# OLYMPUS v0.0.25, "Hold to hold": the build sheet

Written 2026-11-19 for the round's five implementers (A to E) and the lead, who integrates. It is the contract between roles that build in parallel without talking. It sits on **v0.0.24 as integrated**: the tree `62b0d9021bb885a12af3cd71c7684a7c34ead7ef` (`.run/v025/v024-snapshot.tree`, given as `.run/v025/v024-snapshot.patch` on the v0.0.23 tag) and `.run/v024/integrate.md`: F100 to F123, `GAUGE_LAST` 123, house-done 375 rows, the voice synthesis removed whole, every line a text bubble. **Checked against that tree on 2026-11-19 (§14)**: every name, file and function below is the snapshot's or is marked new. Where v0.0.24 as tagged differs from the snapshot, the code decides, stage 0 says so in `.run/v025/lead.md`, and the role adapts.

It is merged from three lens notes, all in `.run/v025-design/`: **play.md** (the play lens: the lane, the drill, the #2, the words, the gauges; **PL§n**), **place.md** (the place and the look; **PC§n**) and **carried.md** (what v0.0.24 leaves open, the known reds, the runner; **CA§n**, items **C1** to **C6**). Where this sheet is silent, the docs decide: DESIGN.md and the user's rules first, then TECH §1.3, then the sections cited, then the lens notes ("as designed" means their mechanism, constants and tests stand unless this sheet changes them). My own choices are marked (my call). Every conflict between the lenses, with v0.0.24's sheet and with the docs is settled in §0.

**Lines.** The lenses read main at v0.0.23 (`e8e4f9b`) and the v0.0.24 worktrees; the check (§14) read the snapshot, and its line pointers are the snapshot's. **Every hunk is named by its function**; a line is only ever a pointer.

## The release in a page

ROADMAP §4.2's row 0.0.7e, `test-zerocqb` "Hold to hold": ship close quarters at micro-g on mag boots in the Wreck at Phobos (PLACES §5.7), by COMBAT §14.5 and §14.8 as written (anchor before you fire, six faces, hold to hold, feet aft), the `void` family's first beats (COMBAT §25.3), BODY §16.6, WEAPONS §7.8. The road is the user's: "now to bring this gameplay smoothly to CQB room clearing in full G, then ship CQB in microgravity and grav boots, and to real combat with enemies" (2026-11-08), and the order of 2026-11-17 (the visual overhaul, the anywhere round, then 0.0.7e "Hold to hold", 0.0.7f and 0.0.7g).

**The one idea** (PL's, kept): "Hold to hold" is not a new engine. It is the shoot house's lane (its tower, its #2, its bundles, its pars, its faults, its card, its bots) played on a second set of authored data through the seams v0.0.21 built for exactly this (`op.js`, `assemble.js houseSpecOf`, `planSetOf`, `handling.js seqOf`), selected by one field on the operation record, `ship: 'wreck'`, absent on every house lane, and played as its own scenario `test-zerocqb` (game.js `specOf` refuses two hosts for one scenario). What is new is small and named: one authored area holding the Wreck's two decks 60 m apart in its plan (§0 item 2, as checked), a hatch in a deck or a deckhead, a body standing on the deckhead, three beat kinds, four faults, the tug's pull, the look of things off the deck.

**The lane, as the sergeant lives it** (§9 has the rest):
1. Deck 5 of the Wreck, the brig: you and your #2 locked on your boots in the passage, the cadre's words from the gallery as text bubbles at the compartment's 1MC speaker (no voice: the synthesis is gone).
2. Two cells off the passage, each through a bulkhead hatch: undog, open, in over the coaming, the house's drill on boots at 0.5 m/s, a target on a bulkhead or the deckhead.
3. The trunk: undog the scuttle in the deck, your #2 takes your harness ("Got you."), you go through head and gun first into the hold below, firing from his grip if a man is up ("Pair · braced (#2) · 420 ms"), then plant your boots on the hold's deckhead beside the hatch: you are upside down, and the stage shows it.
4. The hold, hold to hold, never the open middle; down to the deck; the store through its bulkhead hatch. Once in the lane, the siren and "Secure for burn": feet aft on the deck before the yard tug pulls 0.2 G for 3 s.
5. Stop, UNLOAD; the cadre comes aboard through the lock and checks you clear; the hot wash where you stand; the card with the anchor of every first round.

**Before the roles, stage 0 (the lead)** records every pin, lands what moves no tick (two read-only speed-ups, C4, C5, the runner's gates and warm-up), and makes and sends the two new sample sets on day 1.

**The roles**: **A** the Wreck and its places; **B** the body on a face and the void's beats; **C** the lane; **D** the look of things off the deck; **E** the carried fixes on the 1 G house. **Merge order**: stage 0, E, A, B, C, D (§7).

**Ship rules** (my calls):
- Stage 0 and E ship when F124 (nothing moves, but E's two named re-records) is green.
- `test-zerocqb` is on the Tests menu when `zerocqb-nodead` (F125) and F124 are green; else by URL only (the spec's `menu: false`, which `main.js`'s `scenes()` handle filters: the menu is every `SCENE_IDS` scene in `scenes.js` order, so there is no other switch), and the announcement says so.
- The look ships at each set's default until scored (`wreck-faces`, `portrait-faces`, and v0.0.24's waiting sets), named in the announcement.

**The user's rules over every section**: "keep things simple, it's a game. I love the attention do detail, but only if it won't impact gameplay or performance (or introduce so much complexity it creates bugs)" (2026-11-19); "forget voice synthesis, no voices." (2026-11-19: every line is a text bubble at its speaker); "Try keeping rifles looking like rifles even zero G stuff, let's say we use footing to hold recoil" and "the engine needs to support any surface on any part of the system by design" (2026-11-08); "we shouldn't know what's behind closed doors or walls without looking" (2026-11-19, of H2); the look chosen from numbered samples the user scores, the rated sets collapsed at the bottom of the gallery (2026-11-19); "game world is handcrafted" (2026-11-05); test scenes explain nothing beyond their goal line (2026-11-06); nothing pops in or out of view; one quantity, one helper; visuals obey the sim; AZERTY labels on physical codes.

**Kept as built and starred**: "Stack and clear" (★ 2026-11-17) and every pin of v0.0.24 (F124), but for E's two re-records, each with its cause; F1 to F123 never loosened.

**Rules of the round**: as v0.0.24's, with `.run/v025/` for patches and handoffs, `/private/tmp/claude-501/olympus-build/v025/<role>/` for scratch (unmerged patches kept in `.run/v025/`, which survives a reboot), worktrees `git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/v025-<role> v0.0.24` (until the tag is cut: `v0.0.23` with `.run/v025/v024-snapshot.patch` applied, checked to write 62b0d902) with `node_modules` linked and `.run/v025/stage0.patch` applied, removed at the end. Five roles at `JOBS=2` each, `JOBS=1` while the user plays (input idle under 5 minutes, not the server alone); heavy suites wait for the lead's quiet run. A quick file under 3 s × k of CPU. No role commits; the lead integrates and releases.

**Ports**: A 8230, B 8231, C 8232, D 8233, E 8234; reviews 8235 and 8236; the lead 8239; the runner's 8240 to 8249. Kill every server you start.

**Interfaces first**: each role writes §3's exports as stubs, fills them, and tests against its own stub of another role's export until that role merges. Every stub returns today's answer where `ship` is absent (the deck face, no hatch, no Wreck), so a stubbed role moves nothing.

**Integration**: the stage-0 tree the base; each patch cut against the tree the merges before it left (A on E's, B on A's, C on B's, D on C's), applied with `git apply --3way` in the merge order; after each, `QUICK=1 node tests/run.mjs`, `'env-noregress ›'` and the three house pins.

### The items, as built (the lenses' mechanism stands but for what is said here)

1. **"Hold to hold"** (C; PL§3, PL§9). `?play=test-zerocqb`, seed 48213 at 10:00 UTC unless `&seed`/`&hour`, `&tier=` the house's six sheets (the picker's five, the corporal by URL), `&setup=go|trunk|hold|tug` (the tests' starts: at GO; stacked on the trunk with both cells cleared; on the hold's deckhead after the transit; at the tug's warning). The house's lane on the Wreck's spec: the brief, LOAD, MAKE READY (which also wants the boots locked), Standby, GO, the legs, Stop, UNLOAD, SHOW CLEAR, the hot wash, the card, "Again as …". The loadout 'standard' only; `&loadout=` other than it, `&draw`, `&layout`, `&rooms`, `&house` and `&opfor` dropped with a toast ("The Wreck is shot as set, with the standard kit.", my call). The Tests menu's entry after "Secure for burn" (the key's place in `scenes.js` SCENES, which is the menu's order). **As checked**: its own scenario `'test-zerocqb'` (game.js `SCENARIOS` gains it; `specOf` throws "play 'test-shoothouse' at different hosts or environments" for a Phobos scene on the house's scenario), whose fill is `shoothouse.js testZerocqb`, the house's fill with `ship: 'wreck'` (new, beside `testShoothouse`), the body's clock from the spec's site (`lonOfSite(HOUSE_SCENE.site)` is the Wheel's); "Again as …" plays the game's own scenario (`againAsHouse` returns `scenario: 'test-shoothouse'` today); the picker's house rows and bests are gated on `scene.course === 'house'`, not on the scenario's name (`ui/cards/pairs.js houseQuals`, `houseBests`, the kit's code); `&setup=` values `trunk`, `hold`, `tug` added to `core/debug.js SETUPS`.
2. **The Wreck** (A; PC§2 as changed by §0 items 1 to 4). **One authored `deck` area of the site `phobos-void`, `phobos.void.wreck` (code `wk`), holding both decks 60 m apart in its plan** (§0 item 2 as checked): deck 5 at x 0 to 9.2 (the brig: the passage, the start; six 3 × 3 m cells, cells 2 and 5 open, 1, 3, 4 and 6 dogged, drawn and never offered; rooms `wk.d5.*`) and deck 6 at x 60 to 69.2 (the hold, its cargo stacked deck to deckhead; the store; the port collar's lock, dogged until Stop; rooms `wk.d6.*`), each room carrying `deck: 5 | 6`. The 60 m is MAX_VIEW_M's 48 m window and a margin (render/scale.js): from anywhere on one deck the other is never in the picture. Each deck 9.2 × 7.2 m inside, `ceilingM` 2.2, every face `plateGrid` with the holds by rule (A of v0.0.24's `holds`), the standing walls drawn to the deckhead (`look.wallsToCeiling`: the cutaway's standing runs at the room's `ceilingM`, 2.2, not WALL_H_M 2.8; the cut runs stay CUT_H_M). The trunk joins them: a scuttle in deck 5's deck at (4.6, 3.6) over a scuttle in deck 6's deckhead at (64.6, 3.6), Ø 0.8 m. The bulkhead hatches are openings of kind `'door'` with `leaf: 'hatch'`, `lock: true` (the dogs), `dogs: 4`, `coamingM: 0.3` (an opening's state is only `'open'` or `'closed'`, `places/model.js setOpening`; a dogged hatch is a locked door, undogged by `combat/op.js breakOpening`, which `bundle.js lockedOf` reads). Set A's ten stands (§5). Frozen literals in `src/data/places/wreck.js`, each deck written in its own deck frame and offset into the area's by the deck's origin, its sockets named by face (PC call 1). `phobos-void`'s `areas` and `places/areas.js AREA_LIST` gain it. Plans: the cells and the store derived by `derive.js` and committed as data; the hold, entered from its deckhead, authored with no door (`room.js derive` takes `P.gate`, a line at the scuttle, and its `threshold` the plant point: a deck hatch is no line in the plane).
3. **The transit** (B; PL§6). At the trunk, the `void` beats: the stack round the scuttle on boots, `undog` (1.5 s), `open` (0.5 s), the #2's `brace` ("Got you."), your `hatch` beat (1.0 s × the Zero-g pace, 1.3 s for the sergeant; a Zero-g roll at DC 6, a miss adding 0.2 s a point, never a drift: PL's call), the deck changed with the team by A's `crossHatch` as your eyes pass the deck's plane (one tick: every carried body moved by the trunk's offset, `$px`/`$pz` set with it so nothing glides 60 m, the fact `hatch` for the view's cut; no area changes, so no `area-enter`, no `syncActors`, no `R.area` to keep), a `scan` from the coaming, then your `plant` (`onFace` 'deckhead' beside the scuttle and the boots locked, the transit ended at rest: A's `bootsLockWhy` refuses a drifting lock); the #2's `let` ("Through.") on your plant or 0.2 s after your first round, his own `hatch` and `plant` on the scuttle's other side.
4. **Anchor before you fire** (B rows, C card; PL§5). Every shot row's label carries the footing it will be fired from and its time from v0.0.24's table ("Pair · braced (#2) · 420 ms", "Pair · mag boots · 444 ms", "Pair · one-handed, a hand on the hold −4", "Single · floating −6 · 763 ms": offered, never struck). `houseShot` records each round's anchor (`anchorOf` at the round) beside its row.
5. **The body's face** (B; PL§5, PC§3.2). **`actor.onFace`** (not `face`: an actor's `face` is already its facing, 'up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right', read by `move.js faceOf`, `loco.js`, `portals.js moveTo`): absent on the deck, `'deckhead'` on the deckhead (people stand on these two only this round; boards on all six). On the deckhead the free-fall height `actor.floatY` (v0.0.24's review of A to C: the centre of mass over the deck; `actor.y` stays the floor a body stands on, which the hit model and the blast read as the feet) is `ceilingM − FREEFALL.FLOAT_Y_M`, 1.2 m in the Wreck; `actor.y` is never written there. "Boots to the deckhead" and "Boots to the deck" (1.5 s: release 300, tuck and turn 800, lock 400; from floating within reach of a face, 1.2 s: the tuck and the lock) are the `onface` beat, anchored 'handhold' throughout. A body inverted on the deckhead spans 0.45 to 2.2 m, one on the deck 0 to 1.75 m (`arms/carry.js SPAN_M.stand` [0, 1.75], mirrored from the ceiling: one helper, `bodySpanOf`), they overlap by 1.30 m, so **one nav grid, one sight grid and one collision serve both faces** (PL [computed]). The keys on the deckhead move you as the screen shows, never mirrored. Under the tug (0.05 to 0.3 G) a booted body on the deckhead reads footing 'magWalk' (`footing.js footingAt`'s low-g branch gives 'bound' today, a walk on the face the g pulls you off).
6. **Hold to hold** (B, C; PL§5). Push-off (v0.0.24 B's) is the keys' only, never a drill row. **The open middle** is footing 'float' with no hold within `FREEFALL.REACH_M` 0.8 m (`holdNear`) and no bulkhead or fixture face within it in the plane, for over `OPEN_MS` 1,000 ms while the lane is hot in a compartment not yet called clear: fault 'open', "Get on a face! Hold to hold.". The deck and the deckhead never count for the fault (in 2.2 m they are always in reach, and it would never fire). They count for the push only: in a compartment of `PUSH_LOW_CEIL_M` 2.4 m or less, `freefall.js pushFrom` gives 'deck' to a floating body (it reads `floatY` only today, so a body off the deck with no wall behind it has nothing), so a floating body is never a dead end. (`pushable` is the footing's test, float or a hand's hold, and is not changed.)
7. **Targets on every face** (A data, C lane, D look). A stand gains **`onFace`** (one of six: 'deck', 'deckhead', 'port', 'starboard', 'dorsal', 'ventral'; absent the deck; not `face`, which is a turner's painted face, 'threat' | 'noshoot' | 'armoured' | 'hostage', nor `mount`, a fixture's 'wall' | 'desk'), `y` (its centre's height; `turnerTargets` already reads `T.y ?? 1.35`) and `pop` (a pop-up); its base on the face, its board's centre out from a bulkhead as a man standing on it would be (0.9 m). Stand ids keep the house's form, the leg's number then a letter (`two.js legOf`, `opfor.js legIndex`, `tests/flawless.mjs legOfStand` and `main.js standWords` read `stand[0]`): 1a, 1b (cell 2), 2a, 2b (cell 5), 3a to 3d (the hold), 4a, 4b (the store); the names C2a, H1 … are the card's words only. A pop-up rises from flat on its face in `POPUP_MS` 400 (my call), drawn by `popupPixels`, on the deckhead hanging head down. One area holds both decks, so no area filter is needed anywhere: a board on the other deck is 60 m off and out of every sight line.
8. **The look off the deck** (D; PC§3). Everything off the deck is drawn at its true height (VIEWS §2.1's projection, v0.0.24's float rule), its standing card turned by its face in quarter turns and flips only (`faceCard`, 24 rows; one instance matrix; no new atlas cell, program or draw), through the tumble's 45° frame between faces so nothing pops; one helper `heightLookOf(yM)` gives the float pick's scale and shadow to every body off the deck. **As checked**: it is the rule of `render/view.js`'s figure-loop closure `floatOf(a, fig)` (:596) and `FLOAT_SCALE_FROM_M` 0.5, `FLOAT_SCALE_K` 1.25 (:257) factored out, no new number; it reads `floatY` (the closure still reads `a.y`, the floor: integrate.md §8 says a floater is drawn at the deck's height today), and a body with `onFace` set is drawn planted on its face, turned by `faceCard`, never in the float frames. K-b (the overhead's footprint dashed on the deck below), T-a, P-a, H-a, B-a, X-a until scored.
9. **Black until seen** (A, D; PC§4). The scene's `familiar: 'walls'` (read by `known.js familiarRule` by the game's scenario, which is why the scene has its own): `familiarOf` false on the Wreck's area, `footprintOf` returning `{ rect, fixed, walls }` (the walls' rects, new), and `render/known.js` `begin` marking `footprint.walls` with `WALL_CELLS` (it marks `rect`'s outside and `fixed` only today): every wall cell and its ring known at the start, every compartment the unknown's colour (U1, or the user's `house-unknown` pick) until seen; its boards and men by v0.0.23's rules ("nobody before seen"). A cell is deck to deckhead, one bit. No vertical sight cone (PL: in 2.2 m a deckhead point 2 m off is 17° up from the eyes [computed]).
10. **Secure for burn** (C's lane, B's row; PL§3). C of v0.0.24's profile set at GO by `gravity.js setProfile(state, [TUG])` (its `t0Ms` the clock at the call, so the GO's ms; `atS` is the onset, the warning `warnS` before it): `{ kind: 'burn', toG: 0.2, atS: [60, 150], warnS: 15, holdS: 3 }`, drawn from the seed in whole seconds; the siren, the 1MC's own words (`data/onemc.js warnWords('burn', 15)`, `END.burn` "Burn complete. Coasting."); the drill suspends from the warning to the end (as at a contact). T's first offer is "Feet aft" (rule 'aft'). At the onset `gravity.js throwOne` lets a booted body ride (0.2 G under `BRACE_G` 1.5) and a hand on a hold hold (under `HOLD_MAX_G` 1); the Wreck's lane faults a body booted on the deckhead 'aft' ("Feet aft! Boots on the deck."), which hangs (205 N against 600 N [computed]); a floating body falls from its `floatY` under the 0.5 G/s ramp: from 1.0 m (the plane's float height) 1.97 m/s after 1.20 s, from 1.2 m (pushed off the deckhead) 2.16 m/s after 1.30 s (the snapshot's `fallOf`, [computed]; the lens's 2.26 m/s was 1.3 m at a sharp onset), both over `LAND_MS` 1.5, carded by `impactOf`. **The window** (my call, as checked): the steel copy's sergeant takes 107.55 s for house 1 on boots, so a fast sheet may end the Wreck before an onset at 150 s; C measures the honest tier one's lane on its first build and sets `atS`'s upper bound to that lane less 30 s (never under 60), and F131 counts a lane that ends before its onset as a failure.
11. **Every line a bubble** (C words, D placement; PL§8). The cadre is in the Shed's gallery: his lines from the brief to Stop are bubbles at the 1MC speaker of your compartment (a fixture on every compartment's deckhead); your #2's at him; the 1MC's own at the same speaker. The text is always upright. **As checked**: a bubble's head is `main.js speakerHud`'s `headOf` (a person's actor at a fixed 1.8 m, else the fact's `at`, else none; the 1MC with no `at` at the picture's top), fed by `bus.on('say')`; `plaque.js placeBubbles` only places what `headOf` gives. So the placement is D's two hunks in main.js: `bus.on('say')` gives a speaker's line (the 1MC's, `who` null) and the line of a speaker with no actor on the stage (the cadre in the gallery) the `at` of the speaker fixture in your compartment (the area's `speakers`, A's data), and `headOf` takes a person's head height from `bodySpanOf` (an inverted man's head is at 0.45 m). Without it the cadre's lines have no bubble at all (`headOf` returns null for a `who` with no actor). No plaque.js hunk for D.
12. **A man upside down to you** (D; PC§5). `seenOf` gains `roll` (quarter turns between his up and yours), in the key only when it is not 0, so every shipped key is the same string; R-a turns the card (and its marks) by it; your own I and C cards stay upright.

Aspects: anchor, faces, pace, team, panel, feel, ★.

## 0. The cross-check (every conflict settled)

**Between the lenses:**

1. **Which decks, which way** (PL: decks 1 to 3, the start on the command deck, two transits down; PC: decks 6 and 5 by the port collar, the trunk up). **Settled: decks 5 then 6, one transit down** (my call). The brig first (cells off a passage are the house's rooms off a hall, so the bulkhead hatches reuse the house's drill whole), then down the trunk head first into the hold (PL's transit and brace, the geometry that makes the buddy brace work: the #2 standing on the deck at the coaming reaches your harness; going up through a deckhead from a deck needs a face change first and puts the brace out of reach), then the store. One area holding both decks (item 2), one transit, four compartment legs (PL's count, the house's four due slots: 450, 495, 540, 585 s; the Wreck has **no hall leg**: `two.js legsOf(H)` is `[...H.rooms, H.hall]`, and `shoothouse.js legDueMs` counts `legsOf(H).length`, so with `H.hall` null and four rooms the slots are those four; with a hall leg they would be five, from 405 s).
2. **One area, two decks, one writer** (as checked, my call: the sheet's fallback made the default). The lenses made the decks two areas; the snapshot reads one lane area in too many places for that to be simple: `people/place.js actorsStep` re-makes the actors list (new ids, every actor field lost: the #2's anchor, boots, path) whenever `state.actors.area` is not the live area; `portals.js moveTo` is the player's only area writer (its facts, the autosave, the log); `render/view.js` draws the house's boards only while `state.armoury.range.area` is the live area; the boards are read raw from `R.turners` in 24 files (contact, the #2's brain, the instinct), with no area on them; `op.js inLane`, `shooting.js inHouse`, `room.js derive`, `zones.js zonesOf` and `assemble.js plansOfArea` each take a plan set's one `area`; `houseSpecOf(state).area` feeds the fill, `zoneAt` and the doors' arcs. So **the Wreck is one area, `phobos.void.wreck`, its decks 60 m apart in its plan** (more than `render/scale.js MAX_VIEW_M`'s 48 m window: the other deck is never in the picture), and every one of those readers works unchanged. `places/hatch.js crossHatch(state, bus, hatchId, pids)` (A, new) is the only writer of a deck change: every carried body moved by the trunk's offset in one tick, `$px`/`$pz` with it (no glide), the fact `hatch` (the view's cut, D); it writes no `onFace` (B's `plant` beat does, through `setOnFace`, the field's one writer), so A's patch needs nothing of B's. It is called by the `hatch` beat only: no portal band on the height axis (PC's `band: { axis: 'y' }` dropped, my call), since nothing else crosses a deck hatch this round (a floating body drifts in the plane, a walker meets the open scuttle as a blocked cell). A ship of many areas crossed by its hatches is the drawn Wreck's, 0.5.

VOID_MUSCLE (its muscle's labels by rung) = { 0: ['Stack on the hatch', 'Undog the hatch', 'Open the hatch', 'Through the hatch', 'Boots to the deckhead'],

## 9. Acceptance: what the user must feel

1. **The Tests menu's "Hold to hold"**: the goal line, then the cadre's bubble at the 1MC speaker over your head; "0.00 G · on mag boots" on the strip; the boots' clank on the plate.
2. **The brig's two cells**: undog, open, over the coaming, the house's drill at the boots' pace; a man on the bulkhead standing out of it, a pop-up dropping from the deckhead; no wall, body or doorway hold that the house would not have.
3. **The trunk**: "Got you."; head and gun first into the hold; the row says "braced (#2) · 420 ms" and the pair goes in from his grip; then the plant, and you on the hold's deckhead, upside down, read at once (K's pick), your #2 beside the hatch on its other side.
4. **The hold**: the man behind the hatch on the deckhead is your #2's; "Compartment clear!"; down to the deck; a push-off across the open middle (if you try it) faulted before you reach the far side.
5. **The siren and "Secure for burn"**: T's first offer "Feet aft"; boots on the deck in time; the tug's 0.2 G felt as a lurch on the G line; a man left floating lands at the speed the card says.
6. **The store**: the armoured pop-up on the starboard bulkhead, the hostage card on the deck; "Deck six clear!".
7. **Stop**: the cadre comes in through the lock, checks you clear; the hot wash where you stand; the card with every first round's anchor, "FIRED FLOATING: NONE", "FEET AFT IN … S".
8. **Nothing seen before you look**: each cell and the hold black until you see into them, their walls drawn from the start.
9. **On the 1 G house**: your #2 never holds you in a doorway on a drawn house; the P-12 in your hands on LOAD and SHOW CLEAR; the two plaques apart.

**For the integrator** (as v0.0.24's): F124 after stage 0 and each merge; `QUICK=1 node tests/run.mjs` after each; the gauges never loosened (`'house-flawless-quick ›'`, `'house-flawless-keys ›'` all MET); `game-upgrade` loads every save to v0.0.24's; F60, F133 and `?bench=wreck` PASS on a quiet machine, the user judging Windows; a browser smoke on :8239 (`?play=test-zerocqb&tier=private` by the keys to the card; `&tier=sgt` by T; `&setup=tug`; `&setup=hold` on another seed; no page error, console error or failed request, the server killed after); the heavy suites once on a quiet machine after the last merge (`env-noregress`, `zerocqb-nodead`, `zerocqb-flawless`, `zerocqb-pin`, `ui-zerocqb`, the three house pins, `house-swings`, `GATES=1`'s four, v0.0.24's heavy suites); `house-done` with every row F1 to F137.

**The body (B)**
20. **`actor.face` is the facing** ('up', 'down', 'left', 'right'; `move.js faceOf`, `loco.js`, `moveTo`), a turner's `face` its paint, a fixture's `mount` 'wall' | 'desk': the face a body or board stands on is **`onFace`**, B's readers `onFaceOf`, `setOnFace`, the beat kind `onface` (items 5, 7, §0 item 11, §3.2, §5, §6).
21. **`floatY`, not `y`** (v0.0.24's review of A to C): `actor.y` is the floor, read as the feet by `arms/penetrate.js` and `combat/burst.js`; on the deckhead `floatY` is `ceilingM − FLOAT_Y_M` and `y` absent; `bodySpanOf` is built on `arms/carry.js SPAN_M` and B gains hunks in `penetrate.js` and `burst.js` (removed from the read-only list) (item 5, §1 B, §3.2).
22. `footing.js bootsLockWhy` refuses a lock drifting or with `floatY` over 1.01 m: B's hunk measures from the face locked on, and the transit ends at rest before the plant (§0 item 19, item 3).
23. Under the tug `footingAt`'s low-g branch reads 'bound' for a booted body: on the deckhead it reads 'magWalk' (item 5, §3.2).
24. `freefall.js pushable` is the footing's test; the reach is `pushFrom`: the low-compartment rule goes there, and the open middle counts holds and bulkhead faces only (with the deck and deckhead in reach it could never fire) (item 6, §3.2, F127's test, question 6).
25. **The brace across the trunk**: `heldBy`'s 'buddy' measures the pair within `BUDDY_M`, and after the deck change they are 60 m apart in the plan, so the brace names the trunk (`anchorVia`) and is measured through it (§3.2, risk 7, `zerocqb-two`).
26. The void catalogue takes `ENTER_AND_CLEAR`'s shape (`VOID_DRILL`, beats by `k`), read through one `defOf` beside `bundleDef` and `MUSCLE`; `DRILL_FAMILIES` already lists 'hatch' and 'void' (§0 item 30, §1 B, §3.2).
27. `BARRACKS_LINES` is every `BASE_RULES` and `GROOM_RULES` id, so B's 'aft' would join it: stage 0 leaves out 'aft' with 'anchor' (§2 step 3, §1 stage 0).

**The look (D)**
28. **Bubbles**: a bubble's head is `main.js speakerHud`'s `headOf` (a person at a fixed 1.8 m, else the fact's `at`, else none) fed by `bus.on('say')`; `placeBubbles` only places. D's hunks move from `plaque.js` to those two in main.js, and without them the cadre's lines from the gallery have no bubble (no actor, no `at`) (item 11, §0 item 22, §1 D, §3.4; `plaque.js` is E's alone).
29. **`heightLookOf`** is the view's closure `floatOf(a, fig)` and `FLOAT_SCALE_FROM_M`, `FLOAT_SCALE_K` factored out; it still reads `a.y` (integrate.md §8), so D reads the lift `max(0, floatY − FLOAT_Y_M)` and a body with `onFace` is drawn planted; `ui-anchors`' raised float is re-read with its cause (item 8, §0 item 26a, §3.4, `wreck-look`, Kept, risk 8).
30. The anchors' marker (`render/range.js anchorPixels`) is drawn only on the anchors course (`look.js rangeLook`'s `anchorsLook`): D's `rangeLook` hunk draws the brace and the holds in the Wreck; `look.js` is shared with E's `gunLook` (§1 D, the table).
31. The deck switch's wipe runs on `hatch` (the existing cut is `holdCut` on `area-enter`, never posted inside one area) (§0 item 14, §3.4).

**Names and files corrected**
32. `anchorAction` is `arms/shooting.js`', not `footing.js`'; `adminRun` is `arms/sidearm.js`'; `pistolCheck` and `pistolMag` are `art/figures/poses.js` frames; `warnWords`, `WARN`, `END` are `data/onemc.js`'; `floatOf` is B's `freefall.js` export (and a view closure of the same name); `seen-lookkeys.json` is `tests/seen-lookkeys.json`; `slideRect` exists (`plaque.js` :731) and C3 is a hunk in it (§2 step 0, §1 E, §3.5).

34. The read-only list gains `portals.js`, `people/place.js`, `zones.js` and `plaque.js` but `slideRect`; `burst.js` leaves it (B) (§1).
35. The samples: `void-look` is still unsent (integrate.md §9) and waits with `float-look`, `mag-boots`, `house-unknown`; group letters repeat across sets, keyed by set in "Copy my picks" (§10).

**Disjoint and buildable**: every file has one owner or functions apart (the table: `bundle.js` B and E; `shoothouse.js` stage 0 and C; `room.js` stage 0 and C; `two.js` B and C's one line; `look.js` D and E; `main.js` C and D, merged by the lead; `known.js` A, `render/known.js` D).
